Interesting! The toplevel is `/home/agent/repos/pre-commit`, and `/root/repos/pre-commit` is presumably a symlink (or bind). The HEAD commit is `1d59698 wip(edit): tests/git_test.py` — meaning my edits were auto-committed! The environment apparently commits each edit? Wait, the initial `git log` showed `7b88c63 Merge pull request...`. Now HEAD is `1d59698 wip(edit)`. So the edit tool created commits. Interesting — that's the harness behavior.

Wait, but the task says "Work from the commit that is checked out". The starting commit was 7b88c63. Now there are new commits 0359e43, 1d59698. Did my edits get auto-committed by the environment? The git log earlier (before edits) showed 7b88c63. Then my `edit` calls created commits. Hmm, that's the "tree" mechanism perhaps. But `submit` captures the working tree, so committed or not doesn't matter.

Actually wait, let me re-examine. The first edit I did on git.py. Then `git log --oneline -3` was run at the very start, showing 7b88c63. Then I made edits. The environment auto-commits edits (wip(edit)). That's fine — the tree content is what matters.

But there's a concern: the submit refuses "when the tree is unchanged from the starting commit". The tree has changed, so fine.

Hmm, but actually I should double check that the harness auto-committing is okay. The spec says ".senior-dev/ and git-ignored paths are excluded from the answer. Everything else in the working tree, committed or not, is part of what you submit." So committed changes are included. Good.

Now let me verify the current working tree content is what I want. `git show HEAD:pre_commit/git.py` has the fix. Good.

Wait, but it says `1d59698 wip(edit): tests/git_test.py` and `0359e43 wip(edit): tests/git_test.py`. There's no commit for git.py edit? The first edit was git.py. Hmm, both commits mention tests/git_test.py. Maybe commits are per-edit and messages are odd. Anyway.

Let me check `git show --stat` of these commits.
